Their first (unreleased) album was MFKR (I call it Motherfucker, it's really Mate Feed Kill Repeat), and it was all demo tracks and had a different vocalist. Then Corey came in and Slipknot released the Self-Titled album and they took off. Wait and Bleed, Surfacing, and many others were absolute hits on the album.

Then comes Iowa, one of their darkest albums. Many regard it as the best, and I'd say it's definitely up there. The reason why it's more aggressive is because the band members were all in really dark places at the time. Corey himself has one hell of a story, going from homeless to metal hero. Songs like Gently, My Plague, Skin Ticket, Iowa, they all put blinding anger and rage into words and sound incredibly well, and that's why I think it's one of their most popular albums.

Then, after that, came Vol. 3. It had a different production value due to a new producer I believe, and it had some good songs on it like Vermillion and (I think) The Blister Exists. Duality was another hit that has a crazy music video, if you've never seen it. It has a good mix of melodic tunes and the metal we know and love.

After that album came All Hope is Gone, and this is where I think Slipknot made a big turning point where Corey really nailed down his vocals and they went from "Great band" to "Legendary" status. Many of the songs from that album were fantastic, in my opinion.

However, the band was eventually hit with Paul's death, and you had their 2015 album come out as a tribute to him. I started listening to Slipknot in 2017, and this one is what got me into them.

They just released a new album back in August, and it's damn good. More on the experimental side, but if it's experimental I want more of it.
